salesLanguage.headline: NHD-150-RX: moves AV around the building using the network
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when sources and displays are spread out, the customer needs flexible routing, or the system may grow over time.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It turns AV into a more flexible system where content can be routed to different places without redesigning fixed cabling every time.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Campuses, sports bars, casinos, command rooms, education buildings and large distributed AV systems.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Sell the flexibility and future-proofing, then validate the network design.
talkTrack: It is strongest when the system needs expansion, many endpoints, or routing across distance.
It depends on the network, so switch selection and commissioning matter.
It is not automatically the best option for every multi-display room.
discoveryPrompts: How many sources and displays are needed now and later?
Is there a dedicated AV network or will one be provided?
Does the customer need video wall, multiview, USB, Dante or control integration?
positioningNotes: Use for flexible and expandable systems, not simply because there are multiple screens.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not use AV-over-IP to overcomplicate a small fixed room when a matrix or HDBaseT solution fits better.
marketApplications: Distributed AV routing, video wall, multiview or AVoIP transport

systemIntegrator.label: SI / installer
systemIntegrator.headline: NHD-150-RX: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to confirm endpoint count, switch requirements, VLAN or dedicated AV network design, controller placement and commissioning responsibility.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around AVoIP, NetworkHD 100, 1G Ethernet, HDMI before finalising the design.
Confirm what connects locally, what leaves the room, and which accessories or endpoints are required.
Check USB class, power method, control path and firmware notes before treating the product as a like-for-like substitute.
discoveryPrompts: Where will the product physically live: table, wall, display, rack, lectern or network closet?
What cable type, distance and route are available between each endpoint?
Which products, receivers, USB devices, controllers or network switches must be present for this to work?
How many sources and displays are needed now and later?
Is there a dedicated AV network or will one be provided?
positioningNotes: Good installer language should make dependencies visible before a quote is issued.
Call out install risk early when the product depends on USB bandwidth, network design, endpoint pairing or control integration.
Use for flexible and expandable systems, not simply because there are multiple screens.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not imply it is plug-and-play where cable distance, USB class, endpoint compatibility, network design or control programming still needs validation.
Do not use AV-over-IP to overcomplicate a small fixed room when a matrix or HDBaseT solution fits better.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: NHD-150-RX: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to validate why AV-over-IP is justified: flexibility, expansion, distributed locations, multiview, video wall, USB, Dante or control integration.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?

Is there a dedicated AV network or will one be provided?
